Hi Hannah,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — CartGo is excited about Redwood's latency profile. Before we progress to procurement + SOW, procurement asked for a written clarification on how billing units map between the older Chat Completions endpoints, the newer Responses endpoint, and any other legacy endpoints we should be aware of.

Two asks from our side:
- A short mapping showing how tokens or "billing units" are computed for each endpoint (example math for a 1M input + 200k output token month).
- A baseline hosted rate card PDF with list prices for the endpoints and any common model families, plus typical discount bands for committed usage.

Can you send that and flag any gotchas for customers migrating from the legacy chat endpoint to Responses?

Appreciate it,
Alec

From: hannah_schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>

Alec — thanks, quick reply below and I attached our baseline rate card PDF (Redwood_Baseline_Ratecard_Q4_2026.pdf). Long-form guidance in the attachment; short answers here so you can share with procurement.

1) Endpoint billing model (short):
- Legacy Chat Completions: billed strictly per token (input + output) using model-specific per-token rates. Example: list rate = $0.018 / 1k input tokens, $0.024 / 1k output tokens for family X.
- Responses (new unified endpoint): billed per token as well, but we normalize structured responses and function-call payloads differently — for quoting we translate to an internal "billing unit" that accounts for small-requests overhead. Practically, a Responses call with short metadata + 1k output tokens will round to the same token billing as Chat for most models; differences appear when you rely heavily on function calls or large structured tool outputs.
- Streaming vs non-streaming: tokens are counted the same; streaming only affects latency and practical cost due to prefix caching, not the unit math.

2) How we present it on invoices:
- We include: endpoint name, model, raw token counts (in/out), and the converted billing units for that invoice line so customers can reconcile to logs.

3) Conversion example (1M input + 200k output tokens month) using model family X (list rates shown; substitute if you use family Y):
- Chat Completions: 1,200,000 total tokens -> 1,200 * ($0.018 / 1k input averaged) ~ $21.60 (input) + 240 * ($0.024 / 1k output) ~ $5.76 -> ~$27.36 monthly at list.
- Responses: token count identical in most payloads -> charges end up within ~1-3% of Chat math; difference comes from metadata/tool payloads. For conservative planning we recommend mapping 1 Responses token ~= 1 Chat token for budgeting.

4) Migration gotchas:
- Function/tool outputs: Responses returns structured items that may cause higher tokenization in edge cases; run sample traces.
- Model family mapping: some older models on legacy endpoints have different per-token pricing — see rate card.

5) Next steps: I attached the baseline rate card PDF and a draft SOW stub for procurement (CartGo_Draft_SOW_v1.pdf). If procurement wants a single-line price per 1M tokens for easy budgetary comparison, say so and I can provide a one-page mapping at list + two discount bands (committed / enterprise).

Best,
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

- CartGo looks like a high-volume candidate; initial usage signals point to ~15M tokens/mo.
- Recommend we offer: 12% off list for a 6-month committed baseline at $25k/mo (monthly commit), or 20% off for a 12-month commit at $50k/mo.
- For Responses migration support, carve out 3 dedicated migration run-hours with a Solutions-engineer credit.
- Important: confirm whether they require an "endpoint parity" SLA for legacy -> Responses; that affects the SOW language and possibly pricing.

Hannah: if you're comfortable, propose the 6-month 12% band first to procurement and flag the 12-month 20% as an escalation for legal/finance.

Karthik

3) Pilot SOW: attached draft SOW (CartGo_Draft_SOW_v1.pdf). If procurement is comfortable, we'll send a DocuSign request once you confirm the commit band. Link will be created by Legal after you tell us whether you want 6- or 12-month.

Deliverables timeline: one-page normalized pricing table + updated SOW (with chosen discount band) by 2026-12-14 COB; DocuSign link once discount band is confirmed.

If procurement wants the raw token-count reconciliation instead of the normalized 1M unit line, say that and we'll include both.
